extracted.intended_audience: patients and members of the public who want to peer review Cochrane protocols and systematic reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patients and members of the public on how to peer review Cochrane protocols and reviews, what sections to focus on, what to disclose, and how to submit feedback using Cochrane's systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review means giving feedback on Cochrane protocols and reviews before they are published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers peer review medical research before it is published to check its quality. At Cochrane, patients and the public can give feedback on protocols and reviews prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall quality goals for Cochrane reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback from patients and the public is important to make sure that Cochrane reviews are: easy to understand; written in plain language; relevant and sensitive to patients' needs; helpful to patients and members of the public who need to make decisions about health care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cochrane wants reviews to address questions important to patients, making reviews more relevant and trustworthy. Reviewers should prioritise these goals when commenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary sections to focus your review on
rubrics_metrics.description: Your review should focus on the following sections: the plain language summary (for example, whether the language can be understood by patients and the public), background, outcomes, implications for practice, implications for research, abstract and synopsis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asking authors to elaborate or add content, remember revisions must remain within the overall word limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word limits
rubrics_metrics.description: All revisions must remain within the overall word limit (12,000 words for reviews and 6000 for protocols).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you ask authors to add text, keep the word limits in mind; aim for concise suggestions or wording changes rather than lengthy additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest disclosure (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: All feedback forms include sections on conflicts of interest and acknowledgements. Reviewers are asked specific questions about potential financial or personal interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer each conflicts question honestly; the forms ask about employment by organizations with financial interest, ownership of commercial organizations, other direct financial interests, personal patents (or pending applications), relationships with authors, and whether you are an author of a study that might be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement preference
rubrics_metrics.description: You have the option to remain anonymous to the authors; authors will be encouraged to acknowledge your contribution but can do so only with your written permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms ask: Do you give permission to be acknowledged as a peer reviewer in the published article? If so, named or anonymous? Also ask about being listed on a Cochrane website and how you wish your name/affiliation to appear if named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol — Background clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the background explain the topic clearly (i.e. are the healthcare need and intervention clear)? Does the background address the hopes and concerns of people considering the treatment? Is it clear “why it is important to do the review”?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not clear, indicate which words or phrases are unclear or suggest alternative descriptions. Focus on clarity for patients/public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol — Objectives clarity and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the objectives of the Cochrane protocol clearly described? Are the objectives relevant, and do you think they would help patients, carers and the public in making a healthcare decision?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unclear or not relevant, indicate which words/phrases need improvement and provide reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol — Types of studies appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it clear what types of studies (e.g. randomised controlled trials, observational studies) are to be used? Are the study designs appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not appropriate, suggest addition or deletion of study designs and explain why from a patient/public perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol — Types of participants coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the proposed participants cover all relevant groups of people who might want to use this treatment?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If groups are missing or should be excluded, identify who else should be included/excluded and why (e.g., age groups, comorbidities, carers' perspectives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol — Types of interventions clarity and appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the study interventions and comparisons/controls clearly described? Are the included interventions appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unclear or inappropriate, explain and provide suggestions to improve description or selection of interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol — Outcome measures relevance to consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the outcome measures (benefits and harms/side effects) the ones that are important to consumers, patients and the public?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight other outcomes that are important to users of this review, including patient-centred outcomes or harms that matter to patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol — Search methods for identification of studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you have any comments on the Search methods for identification of studies section?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide any observations about whether the search approach seems likely to find studies relevant to patients or whether additional sources/populations should be searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol — Data collection and analysis comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you have any comments on the Data collection and analysis section?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on whether planned data collection/analysis will address questions important to patients; note if patient-important outcomes might be missed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol — Declarations of interest (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the Cochrane protocol acknowledge possible interests of the authors (e.g. personal or financial) that could have influenced them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out undeclared interests if known, or note where declarations seem adequate/inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol — Language and style of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the Cochrane protocol reasonably easy to understand? Is the technical language used appropriately, and where possible, explained? Is any language insensitive to consumers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify unclear sections and suggest improvements; propose alternative phrases if language is insensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol — Words requiring further definition
rubrics_metrics.description: List any words that you think need further definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide definitions or suggestions for simpler phrasing where terms are technical or ambiguous for patients/public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol — Additional comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Space for any other comments you may have on the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for broader patient-perspective feedback not covered in other fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review — Title (optional comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note the title has already been peer reviewed and agreed to in the published Cochrane protocol. We therefore do not expect you to comment on the title. If you can suggest an improvement, however, please do so here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only suggest title changes if you have a clear patient-facing wording improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review — Abstract completeness and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there anything mentioned in the Cochrane review that may be important, but is missing from the Abstract? Do you think that the Abstract overstates or understates what was found in the Cochrane review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify omissions or statements that may mislead patients about the magnitude/certainty of effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language summary — Title clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the Plain language summary title reflect the title of the Cochrane review, and is it easy to understand?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not, identify difficult words/phrases or suggest improved wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language summary — Population clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the health problem or issue being addressed stated clearly in the Plain language summary population section?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out ambiguous population descriptions and suggest clearer phrasing (age groups, severity, settings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language summary — Interventions clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the interventions and comparisons/controls examined in the Cochrane review stated clearly and succinctly in this section?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight unclear descriptions and suggest concise plain language alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language summary — Findings clarity (including adverse effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the Plain language summary report the main findings from the Cochrane review clearly and accurately? Does it report on adverse effects or harms?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note omissions of harms or unclear statements about direction/size of effects; suggest clearer presentation for patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language summary — Quality of evidence description
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the Plain language summary describe the overall quality of the evidence, and comment on any issues that could affect the findings of the review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether the summary adequately communicates certainty/limitations in accessible language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language summary — Consistency with abstract and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you think the findings in the Plain Language Summary are consistent with the Abstract and the rest of the Cochrane review? Is anything important missing or overstated/understated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag inconsistencies between sections that could mislead readers and suggest corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language summary — Usefulness for decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you think the Plain language summary would help patients, carers and the public in making a healthcare decision? If not, is anything missing that should be included?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest additions to make the summary more actionable or relevant to patients' decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language summary — Writing style
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the Plain language summary written in plain language and easy to understand? Are sentences too long or wordy? Are there parts that should be rewritten?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out wordy sentences and provide specific rewrites or shorter alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language summary — Terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Are abbreviations, research terms and technical terms avoided or explained? If any terms require clarification, please include them here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List terms to explain or replacement simpler terms; suggest parenthetical explanations if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review — Results format and interpretability
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you understand the format of the results? Is it clear whether the intervention was effective or not?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If results presentation is confusing for patients, suggest ways to clarify (e.g., plain language statements, explicit statements about effectiveness and magnitude).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review — Quality of the evidence and risk of bias reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the results include information about the overall quality of the evidence, and risk of bias?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out missing discussion of certainty or bias that would affect interpretation by patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review — Study funding disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the section ‘Included studies’ and the ‘Characteristics of included studies’ table include details about the funding sources for the studies?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note missing funding information or funding sources that may influence interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review — Discussion balance (harms and benefits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the authors discuss harms as well as benefits? Are the effects of the treatments over- or understated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure harms are reported fairly and suggest language to avoid overstating benefits or downplaying harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review — Author's conclusions: implications for practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Is this section clear and reasonably easy to understand?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether practical implications are framed in ways patients can act on or understand; suggest clearer wording if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review — Author's conclusions: implications for research
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you think the authors have identified the important areas for future research? Are there any missing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight patient-important research questions that are not mentioned, including benefits/harms important to healthcare users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review — Declarations of interest (review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the Cochrane review acknowledge possible interests of the authors (e.g. personal or financial) that could have influenced them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on adequacy of declarations and flag omissions if known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of findings table — Outcome importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you think the outcomes included in the Summary of findings table are the most important outcomes to people with experience of the health condition?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not, list outcomes that matter to patients and suggest they be included or emphasised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and style of writing (review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the Cochrane review reasonably easy to understand? Is the technical language used appropriately, and where possible, explained? Is any language insensitive to patients and the public?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify unclear or insensitive language and suggest patient-friendly alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words requiring further definition (review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please list below any words that you think need further definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete alternative phrasing or definitions for technical terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional comments (review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please add any other comments that you may have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this field for any remaining patient-perspective feedback not covered elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall recommendation categories and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The dropdown Recommendation menu asks you for your overall opinion on the draft review. Choose your recommendation based on the extent of changes you think the authors need to make before the review can be published: Accept – no further changes needed; Minor Revision – some small changes needed; Major Revision – substantial changes needed; Reject – draft review is not suitable for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may wish to complete the rest of the questions before giving your overall recommendation; choose based on patient-facing clarity, relevance, and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus feedback on usefulness to patients/carers/public
rubrics_metrics.description: When giving your feedback, please focus on how useful the review will be to patients, carers and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise comments that improve decision-making utility, clarity, and relevance to lived experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and style of reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Your comments should be respectful and objective and help the authors produce a concise and focused review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can suggest specific wording changes to make the review easier to understand; avoid personal attacks and be constructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing and acceptance procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Please accept your invitation within 7 days or you will be automatically uninvited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitation email contains Accept and Decline links. If you decline or miss the deadline, you will be uninvited. Use the links to go to the Cochrane account login and Editorial Manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to access the draft and submit feedback (Editorial Manager steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Pending Assignments, click View Submission to open a PDF of the draft review (if multiple PDFs, click the link at the top of the list). After reading, click Submit Recommendation to open the online comments form, complete each question, choose an overall recommendation, and Submit Review to Editorial Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can read online or download the PDF. Use Save & Submit Later if you need more time. If you see a warning that not all questions are complete, ensure you have chosen your overall recommendation before proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission: requesting copies of other feedback/responses
rubrics_metrics.description: If you would like to receive a copy of all the feedback on this review from other reviewers, or the authors’ responses to your comments, contact the Cochrane Review Group publishing the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can reply to your invitation email or contact the Cochrane Support team to request these materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and resources availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence Essentials (four-module course) and Conducting an Intervention Review courses are available free for peer reviewers to learn about evidence-based medicine, clinical trials, and Cochrane methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take Evidence Essentials if new to peer review and Cochrane evidence; use Conducting an Intervention Review to understand review methods and research used in Cochrane reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for reviewers with lived experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Because lived experience of healthcare conditions can be emotionally charged, support is available if a review topic is directly relevant to your health status or condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the Patient and Public Involvement Manager or Patient and Public Network Executive for support, advocacy, or other assistance.
